finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl lets an unauthenticated client read arbitrary files via ../ sequences in the f query parameter (e.g. f=../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd).
finding.source: Query parameter 'f' read unvalidated at files.go:12 (r.URL.Query().Get("f"))
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, contents written to response at files.go:18

trace.note: name is taken directly from the attacker-controlled query string with no validation
filepath.Join joins name onto /srv/files and Clean resolves .. segments, so the path can escape root
file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No .. rejection, no Clean-then-prefix check against root, no filepath.Base (only applied in /avatar), no authentication or authorization in the handler or listener. filepath.Join does not reset on a leading / so absolute paths stay under root, but .. escapes it. Verified by reading documented filepath.Join semantics; not executed, because the scratch test was blocked by a permission prompt.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12 reads the query parameter `f` unvalidated, and files.go:13 joins it onto root with filepath.Join and no containment check. The only guard in the file, filepath.Base at files.go:22, is in avatar() and is not on the download() path. No authentication or authorization exists in download(), main() (files.go:31-35), or the :8082 listener.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: files.go:12 takes `f` from the query string, files.go:13 passes it to os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with root="/srv/files" (files.go:9), so `f=../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd, and files.go:18 returns the contents to an anonymous client with no guard in between.

finding.claim: /dl has no authentication or authorization, so anyone who can reach port 8082 can download every file under /srv/files. Needs confirmation whether public access is intended.
finding.source: Any network client reaching the listener; ListenAndServe(":8082") at files.go:34 binds all interfaces over plaintext HTTP
finding.sink: Entire /srv/files tree served via os.ReadFile at files.go:13 and response write at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl route registered with no middleware or auth wrapper
download handler performs no identity or ownership check
file read proceeds for any caller
listener binds all interfaces without TLS

finding.guards_checked: No authentication middleware, no per-file authorization, no per-user scoping, and no listener restriction in the code. Severity depends on whether the service is meant to be public.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /dl route is registered directly at files.go:32 with no middleware. download() at files.go:11-19 performs no identity, ownership, or path-containment check. The only conditional (files.go:14) handles read errors and does not restrict access. The listener at files.go:34 binds ":8082" over plaintext HTTP with no restriction.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: /dl is routed without auth at files.go:32, download() reads an attacker-chosen `f` with no check at files.go:12-13 and writes it at files.go:18, and the server listens on all interfaces without TLS at files.go:34, so any anonymous network client can fetch files. The claim understates the impact: filepath.Join(root, name) at files.go:13 does not contain the path, so `f=../../...` can read files outside /srv/files, limited only by the process's filesystem permissions. The finding should be raised as unauthenticated arbitrary file read (path traversal), not just exposure of /srv/files, and the "is public access intended?" question does not change the result.
